purpose: Controlled copy and source map for the 14 remaining governed Course 1 raster replacement candidates. This file authorizes deterministic candidate production only; it does not authorize learner-facing release.

production.footer: Academic learning visual • Follow current controlled procedures and authorized role boundaries.

assets.title: Hierarchy of Controls & Technician I Boundaries
assets.kicker: CONTROL THE HAZARD AT THE STRONGEST AUTHORIZED LEVEL
assets.purpose: Teach the hierarchy of controls while separating control preference from technician authority.
panels: Elimination & substitution
Remove the hazard or replace it with a lower-hazard option when the authorized process permits.
Engineering controls
Use physical design or isolation controls established by the facility; do not redesign systems independently.
Administrative controls
Follow controlled procedures, scheduling, access rules, training and work practices.
PPE
Use the task-specific PPE required by the hazard assessment, label/SDS and site procedure.
Technician boundary
If the needed control exceeds assigned authority, stop or stabilize as authorized, document and escalate.
assets.boundary: Control effectiveness and authorization are separate questions. A stronger control is not automatically a Technician I decision.

assets.title: PPE & Hazard Communication Decision Map
assets.kicker: TASK → HAZARD INFORMATION → PROCEDURE → REQUIRED PROTECTION
assets.purpose: Connect the assigned task to the controlled information that determines PPE and restrictions.
panels: 1. Identify the assigned task
Confirm the exact material, product, equipment and work activity.
2. Check the hazard basis
Use the employer hazard assessment and the actual conditions of the work.
3. Read label & current SDS
Verify product-specific hazards, precautions, first aid and required protective measures.
4. Check site procedure
Apply facility restrictions, training prerequisites and task authorization.
5. Use required PPE
Inspect, wear, remove and handle PPE according to the controlling instructions.
assets.boundary: This is a decision model, not a universal task-to-PPE chart. Specialized protection is used only under the applicable program and authorization.

assets.title: Cultivation Work-Area Hazard Scan
assets.kicker: SCAN THE ACTUAL AREA BEFORE THE TASK STARTS
assets.purpose: Practice a repeatable work-area scan without implying a universal hazard list.
panels: Pathways & housekeeping
Look for slips, trips, blocked routes, unstable storage and changing work conditions.
Electrical & powered equipment
Check visible condition, cords, wet-location concerns, guards and access boundaries.
Access & physical hazards
Notice ladders, overhead work, sharp edges, pinch points and restricted areas.
Exposure conditions
Check products, dusts, aerosols, residues, heat, noise or other task-relevant exposure cues.
Act on what you find
Use only authorized routine controls; stop and escalate unsafe, changing or out-of-scope conditions.
assets.boundary: Representative examples support a scanning method. The current task, site procedure and actual conditions control the response.

assets.title: Biosecurity Pathway Map
assets.purpose: Show how contamination can move through people, tools, equipment and material pathways.
panels: Source
Plant material, debris, media, water, residues, pests or other contamination sources.
Routes
People, PPE, tools, carts, hoses, containers, surfaces, media and plant movement.
Receiver
A susceptible plant, propagation area, room, clean tool, container or controlled zone.
Interrupt the route
Use the site-defined transition, sanitation, separation and movement controls.
Verify before crossing
A sanitized item can be recontaminated; current status matters at every transition.
assets.boundary: Zone names, traffic direction and transition rules are facility-specific. Use the current zone map and SOP.

assets.title: Cleaning & Disinfection Sequence
assets.kicker: CLEAN FIRST • APPLY THE APPROVED PRODUCT CORRECTLY • VERIFY
assets.purpose: Teach the ordered distinction between debris removal, cleaning, product verification, contact conditions, finishing, inspection and documentation.
panels: 1. Prepare & control the area
Confirm scope, required PPE, material status and what must be protected or removed.
2. Remove gross debris & clean
Physical cleaning comes before the disinfection step where the procedure requires it.
3. Verify the exact product
Use the approved product, current label/instructions, preparation and compatibility requirements.
4. Meet contact conditions
Follow the controlling instructions for application, coverage and required contact conditions.
5. Finish, inspect & document
Complete any required finish step, protect from recontamination, inspect and record the result.
assets.boundary: No universal concentration, contact time, rinse or drying rule is implied. The product label and facility procedure control the exact method.

assets.title: Quarantine, Hold & Restricted-Entry Controls
assets.kicker: DIFFERENT CONTROLS CAN OVERLAP — CLEAR EACH ONE SEPARATELY
assets.purpose: Keep biological isolation, operational hold status and pesticide-entry restrictions conceptually separate.
panels: Quarantine
Separates plant material or an area because biological or pest risk remains unresolved.
Hold
Prevents movement, use, release or further processing while an authorized decision is pending.
Restricted-entry interval
A pesticide-labeling interval that restricts ordinary worker entry where the Worker Protection Standard applies.
Statuses can stack
Releasing one status does not automatically clear another applicable restriction.
Breach response
Stop further movement or exposure, preserve identity and route evidence, document facts and escalate each open decision.
assets.boundary: Release, disposition and worker-entry clearance can come from different authorities or rules. Verify every active control.

assets.title: Controlled SOP / Work-Order Anatomy
assets.kicker: VERIFY THE CURRENT CONTROLLED SOURCE BEFORE ACTING
assets.purpose: Show the information a technician needs to confirm before and during controlled work.
panels: Identity & revision
Confirm the document/work order and its current controlled version.
Prerequisites
Check required training, materials, status, PPE, equipment and preconditions.
Ordered steps
Follow the controlled sequence and any defined decision points.
Acceptance criteria
Know what evidence is required to call a step or task complete.
Records & escalation
Capture required evidence and route exceptions, deviations or out-of-scope conditions correctly.
assets.boundary: The layout is illustrative. The facility’s current controlled source, not memory or an old copy, governs the work.

assets.title: Plant & Material Genealogy
assets.kicker: KEEP IDENTITY CONNECTED THROUGH EVERY CONTROLLED EVENT
assets.purpose: Visualize identity continuity from source material through routine cultivation, movement and disposition events.
panels: Source identity
Begin with the controlled source plant, seed lot, clone batch or other originating material.
Propagation & derived material
Link new plant or material identifiers back to the correct source relationship.
Location & movement
Preserve identity when material changes room, zone, container or process point.
Harvest, samples & containers
Carry the controlled relationship into later material, sample and container records.
Disposition trail
Keep final status and downstream events tied to the correct genealogy rather than relying on appearance or memory.
assets.boundary: Example identifiers are vendor-neutral and illustrative. The facility and applicable program define the actual record fields.

assets.title: Inventory Reconciliation Without Forced Balancing
assets.purpose: Show how physical and recorded evidence are compared without inventing movements or corrections.
panels: 1. Verify identity
Confirm the exact material, lot, plant, container and location being compared.
2. Compare physical vs record
Count or verify what is actually present and compare it with the controlled record.
3. Review recent events
Check authorized movements, transfers, waste, corrections and other relevant records.
4. Preserve the discrepancy
Keep unresolved differences visible; separate confirmed facts from hypotheses.
5. Document & escalate
Use the authorized reconciliation/correction process. Never force the numbers to match.
assets.boundary: A discrepancy is operational information. Record correction requires a valid basis and the controlled process.

assets.title: Authorization & Servicing Boundary
assets.purpose: Separate routine technician actions from technical changes, diagnosis, repair or protected servicing.
panels: Assigned routine work
Continue only when the task is assigned, the procedure is current and required training/authorization is in place.
Routine care
Perform external cleaning, observation, setup or simple checks only when the procedure explicitly permits them.
Stop conditions
Unsafe conditions, failed readiness criteria, unknown status or changing conditions require pause and control.
Servicing boundary
Protected access, stored energy, disassembly, diagnosis, repair, electrical work and calibration transfer to authorized roles.
Escalation
Preserve safe status, record observations and route the issue through the facility’s chain of command.
assets.boundary: A problem does not create permission to troubleshoot beyond scope. Technician I authority comes from assignment, training and controlled procedure.

assets.title: Maintenance-Ready Fault Report
assets.kicker: REPORT VERIFIED CONTEXT — NOT AN UNSUPPORTED DIAGNOSIS
assets.purpose: Provide a supporting fault-report view that preserves useful observations, timing and safe status.
panels: Exact asset & location
Record the equipment identifier, area and process context.
Time-ordered observations
Capture alarm codes, symptoms, visible conditions, sounds or other verified facts with date/time.
Permitted checks
Document only checks the procedure allows and the result of each check.
Operational impact
State what stopped, changed, remained safe or could not be verified.
Safe status & notification
Preserve the required status and use the approved maintenance/escalation channel.
assets.boundary: Keep observations separate from hypotheses. Diagnosis and repair remain with the authorized role.

assets.title: Professional Shift-Handoff Model
assets.kicker: TRANSFER STATUS, EVIDENCE, RISK AND OWNERSHIP
assets.purpose: Retain a concise supporting handoff model alongside the more detailed Lesson 6.2 handoff visual.
panels: Exact identifiers
Use the controlled room, crop, material, lot, equipment and work-order identifiers.
Completed vs open
Separate verified completed work from incomplete, blocked, unknown or pending work.
Current restrictions
State holds, quarantine, equipment status, alarms, safety controls or other active constraints.
Notifications & next actions
Record who was notified, critical timing and the controlled next step without inventing priorities.
Ownership confirmation
Confirm the receiver understands the open items and who owns each unresolved decision.
assets.boundary: A verbal handoff does not override controlled records, current procedures or receiver authorization.

assets.title: Deviation, Exception & Honest Work Status
assets.kicker: DESCRIBE WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED — DO NOT MANUFACTURE COMPLETION
assets.purpose: Teach truthful classification of complete work, planned exceptions, deviations, incomplete work and unknown/unverified status.
panels: Complete
Required steps and acceptance criteria are met and the required evidence exists.
Planned exception
The controlled procedure anticipated the condition and provides an approved alternate path.
Deviation
An unplanned departure from an approved instruction, expected condition or process requires documentation and evaluation.
Incomplete
One or more required steps, records, measurements or acceptance checks are not complete or verified.
Unknown / unverified
Keep uncertainty visible when the evidence does not support a conclusion; hand the open decision forward.
assets.boundary: A missed observation stays missing unless a controlled late-entry or correction process preserves the true timing and status.

assets.title: Cultivation Data-Integrity Record Lifecycle
assets.kicker: MAKE THE RECORD RECONSTRUCTABLE — NOT JUST NEAT
assets.purpose: Show the broader record lifecycle around the more focused controlled-correction visual.
panels: Identity & context
Tie the observation or action to the correct material, asset, location, unit and process point.
Real timing
Record when the activity or observation occurred; preserve later entry timing when a controlled late-entry process is used.
Attribution
Keep creation and changes tied to the responsible person or controlled system.
Transparent correction
Preserve the original entry and an understandable change history using the facility method.
Missing data & handoff
Leave missing information visibly missing and preserve enough context for another qualified person to reconstruct what happened.
assets.boundary: Never backfill a target, estimate or remembered approximation as though it were the original contemporaneous measurement.

supplementalPrimaryConcepts.title: Safety Data Sheet Anatomy
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.kicker: USE THE CURRENT SDS FOR THE ACTUAL PRODUCT IN USE
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.purpose: Give learners a fast map for locating core hazard, first-aid, handling, exposure-control and emergency information without turning a training example into product-specific instructions.
panels: Identification
Confirm product identity, recommended use and supplier information before relying on the document.
Hazard identification
Locate the classified hazards, signal word, pictograms, hazard statements and precautionary statements.
First aid & emergency response
Find first-aid measures and the sections covering fire-fighting and accidental-release information as applicable.
Handling & storage
Check safe handling practices, storage conditions and incompatibilities in the current SDS.
Exposure controls & PPE
Use the exposure-control and personal-protection information together with the employer hazard assessment and site program.
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.boundary: A training SDS is only a navigation example. Product-specific decisions come from the current manufacturer SDS, label and facility HazCom process.

supplementalPrimaryConcepts.title: Controlled Zone Movement & Clean/Dirty Flow
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.kicker: STATUS CAN CHANGE AT EVERY TRANSITION
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.purpose: Provide the second individual biosecurity concept master required by the release manifest.
panels: Read the facility zone map
Use the current site-defined risk zones and transition rules rather than assuming universal room names or traffic direction.
Verify current status
Check the worker, PPE, tool, cart, hose, material and area status before crossing a controlled boundary.
Complete the required transition
Apply the defined sanitation, changeover, separation or access step before moving into the next zone.
Prevent back-contamination
A cleaned or sanitized item can lose that status after new contact; protect it from uncontrolled surfaces and routes.
Stop on uncertainty
When the route, status or required transition cannot be verified, stop movement and use the facility escalation process.
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.boundary: “Clean-to-dirty” is not a universal one-way rule. Direction, backtracking and transition requirements come from the facility’s current risk map and SOP.

supplementalPrimaryConcepts.title: Material Movement Record
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.purpose: Provide the second individual traceability concept master required by the release manifest.
panels: Identity
Record the controlled plant, material, lot, batch or container identifier involved in the move.
From → to
Capture the source and destination needed to reconstruct where the material moved.
Time & event context
Record when the movement occurred and the task, transfer or event that explains it.
Quantity / status
Record the required count, quantity or status information without inventing precision the system does not require.
Attribution & evidence
Keep the move attributable in the facility’s controlled system and preserve any required supporting record.
supplementalPrimaryConcepts.boundary: This is a vendor-neutral evidence model. Exact fields, software and reporting rules are controlled by the facility and applicable program.
